# Bound remaining ordinary Node archive transfers and coupled policy tests

## Current Task402 disposition

This remains an open, repository-maintainer-owned reliability follow-up under the existing [CR-212-04 merits-based decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/212#issuecomment-5896646906). It is not claimed complete by removal of the old inline commands or by successful normal setup.

At accepted PS main `48f4d8a36c8faceee12afac78aaecea0d176125d`, the old sites below have been replaced or deleted. The reachable ordinary download is now in `.github/workflows/Initialize-CiToolchain.ps1`. It has `--connect-timeout 20`, `--max-time 180` and `--retry 2`, but no total retry-duration option. The actual Terraform counterpart at `06ad4f7c9b6847028cafdacf1ae55128d0f2d56c` has the same transfer/retry flags. The separate Copilot setup already has `--retry-max-time 300`. Existing helper tests cover download failure and wrong bytes; they do not prove ordinary Retry-After exhaustion behavior.

A bounded local curl8.5.0 test used a loopback HTTP503 response with Retry-After5. With connection/transfer limits1second and retry2, the process was still sleeping when the harness stopped it at2.005seconds; this is an intentionally stopped run, not a pass. Adding retry-max-time1 produced native exit22 in0.005seconds. This measures curl retry semantics only, not an outage or integrity bypass in the official Node download. [Primary curl documentation](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html#--retry-max-time) explains that max-time resets for each transfer and retry-max-time does not stop an already active transfer.

When this follow-up starts, recheck the current actual download consumers and the shared Terraform initializer. Use the full decision process to choose a useful retry/overall failure budget and coupled negative tests. Preserve archive origin, digest-before-execution, locked runtime selection and native failure handling. Test delayed retries and partial/native failures through the actual caller without a live-service outage. Do not restore retired workflows or add a dependency on completing this cleanup plan.

The historical three-site inventory below records the finding's origin. It is not the current repair locator.

## Historical issue requirements

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->
# Bound the remaining ordinary Node archive transfers

Origin: Claude finding CR-212-04 on [PR212](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/212), validated and selected through the [complete fresh decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/212#issuecomment-5896646906).

At immutable PS head `1a2d0a75e4c5f274c9bdf56587b772549c6c0ecf`, three anonymous Node archive commands lack explicit retry/connect/transfer/retry-duration bounds: `.github/workflows/markdownlint.yml` lines94 and486, and `.github/workflows/pull-request-body-identity.yml` line558. They use the reviewed Node24.18.1 archive and SHA256 `D6C664DF3F3F61458E8C277585571328522D705166723A7C7823A9253A4D15A0`. These are three sites in two files, separate from the two Node24.18.0 ordinary agent/Copilot commands addressed by issue211. The body-identity candidate-blob transfer at line204 already has its own bounds and is not this Node-download finding.

No live outage or integrity bypass is claimed. This is a verified reliability and usable-failure improvement. A connection or transfer stall currently relies on the containing job limit. The change belongs with the ordinary workflow-policy contracts and their trusted admission, rather than expanding the U1-only protected installation in issue211. Existing issue149 does not include this complete two-workflow scope. This deferral was selected on policy-domain, verification and scope merits, not worker time or reviewer availability.

## Scope and constraints

- Inventory all three sites from the current immutable base before implementation. Retain exact runtime versions, archive digests, official URLs, fixed tool resolution, digest-before-execution, credential/config exclusion and nonzero native status handling.
- Choose finite connection, individual transfer and total retry-start bounds with usable failure diagnostics; document the maximum attempt/time behavior. Compare the already bounded U1 pair as evidence, not as permission to copy unrelated runtime pins or policies.
- Update all coupled ordinary workflow-policy constants, contracts, reference fixtures and negative cases. Trace `.github/workflows/Validate-WorkflowPolicy.mjs` and the body-identity validator/admission callers before editing.
- Preserve the existing trust source, path/byte/history limits, job authority, immutable supplies and canonical inactive terminal manifest. Candidate content remains inert during privileged admission. Do not change settings, protection, credentials, package governance, Node versions or unrelated agent roles.
- Use the applicable trusted maintenance mechanism. This issue grants no direct-main installation, force push, administrator bypass or permission to reuse issue211's bounded exception.

## Acceptance and validation

1. All three final Node commands have the selected finite transfer policy. Test missing/asymmetric bounds and native download failures. Include connection/transfer timeout and retry-exhaustion behavior through isolated local fixtures with no production endpoint mutation.
2. Retain digest mismatch rejection before extraction/execution and positive exact-digest behavior. Prove no token or extra authority is introduced.
3. Run affected complete ordinary workflow-policy/body-identity/admission tests, workflow shape checks, PowerShell analysis and applicable hooks. Verify the exact admitted input through the real callers and retain negative results honestly.
4. Complete exact-input external review, fresh independent quality, current-head CI and the normal merge/landed verification lifecycle. A skipped, stale, pending or unavailable result is not success.
5. Publish immutable source/final identities, exact site census, selected limits, actual tests and any deliberately retained differences.

## Ownership, dependencies and reopen condition

The next assigned implementation agent owns this focused follow-up; repository maintainers own its scheduling and final acceptance. Creating it does not commence implementation. Native blocked-by/blocking edges must reflect actual unfinished prerequisites. No such prerequisite is established now; do not add an edge to issue211, issue149 or an umbrella merely for bookkeeping.

Reopen if a final transfer is unbounded, paired policy diverges without evidence, retry/time semantics are misreported, immutable supply verification weakens, or tests fail to cover one of the three sites. Cite this issue from PR212 before closing CR-212-04.

body:
## Problem

The current YAML guide requires a privileged workflow to verify the fetched commit after acquisition. It does not require an immutable event revision as the acquisition source.

A run can fetch `github.ref` after another event moves that ref. The later comparison with `github.sha` detects the mismatch but cannot recover the event commit. The run then fails although the immutable event commit remains valid and retrievable.

## Deferral rationale and trigger

PR #174 did not receive authorization for another protected guide edit. Start this work only after a maintainer explicitly authorizes `.github/instructions/yaml.instructions.md` and the exact rule scope in a new implementation task.

This issue does not provide that authorization. It does not start implementation.

## Affected scope

The future rule applies to GitHub Actions jobs that claim to validate one immutable event commit. It includes privileged `pull_request_target` jobs and similar jobs that fetch or check out Git data.

Keep least privilege, non-forcing fetches, bounded acquisition, and exact post-acquisition commit verification. Do not change the completed workflow repair through this guide task.

## Origin and implemented workflow

- Candidate PR: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174
- Origin thread: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174#discussion_r3834358343
- Disposition reply: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174#discussion_r3834638076
- Implemented workflow commit: `00d380586bb728544bad921f1ab809d49646a89b`
- Implemented workflow tree: `9dbea0305812650d4143df6f8cba8f195881fc12`
- Implemented workflow path: `.github/workflows/devcontainer-ci.yml`

PR #174 already fixes the workflow at the recorded commit and tree. This issue tracks only future guide work.

## Examples

Compliant acquisition uses the immutable event revision as the fetch source.

```yaml
env:
  EXPECTED_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
```

```sh
git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
  "${EXPECTED_REVISION}:refs/remotes/event/target"
actual_revision="$(git rev-parse --verify 'refs/remotes/event/target^{commit}')"
test "$actual_revision" = "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
```

Noncompliant acquisition resolves a mutable ref first and compares the result later.

```yaml
env:
  EXPECTED_REF: ${{ github.ref }}
  EXPECTED_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
```

```sh
git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
  "${EXPECTED_REF}:refs/remotes/event/target"
actual_revision="$(git rev-parse --verify 'refs/remotes/event/target^{commit}')"
test "$actual_revision" = "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
```

The final comparison is necessary, but it is insufficient when acquisition resolves a mutable ref. It detects the race after acquisition instead of preventing it.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] State that an immutable event revision must be the fetch or checkout source.
- [ ] Prohibit mutable-ref acquisition followed only by expected-revision comparison.
- [ ] Preserve the least-privilege, no-force, bounded-fetch, and exact-commit rules.
- [ ] Include one compliant immutable-revision example and one noncompliant mutable-ref example.
- [ ] Record explicit maintainer authorization before changing `.github/instructions/yaml.instructions.md`.
- [ ] Update the guide version and date as its instructions require.
- [ ] Add a ref-move validation fixture that proves immutable acquisition remains deterministic.
- [ ] Verify `.github/workflows/devcontainer-ci.yml` conforms at the recorded commit and tree.
- [ ] Run repository instruction validation, Markdown validation, front-matter YAML parsing, and two clean full pre-commit passes.
- [ ] Record exact commands, native exits, changed paths, Git objects, bytes, and SHA-256 values.

Do not assign this issue, attach it to a project, create a relationship, or link a branch during creation.
title: Require immutable event revisions as workflow acquisition sources

# Artifact generator and verifier: remaining filesystem race and path-identity limitations

## Current disposition

The repository maintainer owns this open residual record. Task379 selects no product repair at this time. Accepted [PR221](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/221) retired the old archive extractor, invocation-context helper, harness and catalog. Their extraction, directory-adoption and two-root alias paths have no remaining consumer. Removal reduces applicability; it does not fix their historical races.

The current `Generate-StyleGuideArtifacts.ps1` and `Test-ExactGitPathSet.ps1` still use paths for some reads, publication and cleanup. Before/after checks do not prove that no transient replacement occurred. The verifier's GUID-named temporary-directory creation and cleanup also have a race surface under a competing-writer threat model. This assessment did not reproduce a supported-caller failure, establish a new untrusted-writer requirement, or prove universal Windows alias/handle identity.

Reassess when a supported current caller reproduces a failure, a deliberate requirement admits concurrent untrusted writers, a concrete usable runtime/API improvement addresses these operations, or a new consumer has materially different authority. A date, version change alone, retired phase name or old test count does not trigger implementation. Start any selected repair with a scoped decision and meaningful tests. Do not recreate deleted helpers merely to close their old findings.

The original findings and measured/unmeasured limits below remain historical evidence. Retired coverage obligations are recorded in [issue156](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/156).

Full validation, options, separate weighted rubrics, scores and selected instructions: [Task379 decisions D92/D93](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/155#issuecomment-5943334454).

## Historical residual record

## Summary

PR #153's fail-closed candidate validator **narrows but does not fully close** a
family of time-of-check/time-of-use (TOCTOU) and path-identity gaps in
`Expand-StyleGuideCandidateArtifact.ps1` and
`Manage-StyleGuideCandidateInvocationContext.ps1`. Each remaining gap has the
same shape: the code proves a path's identity, then acts on it, and a competing
writer acting inside that window — or a Windows alias the canonical spelling
cannot express — can still defeat the proof. Closing any of them requires an
OS-native primitive that portable .NET does not expose and Windows PowerShell
5.1 cannot reach without P/Invoke.

This issue records the residual so it survives PR #153's merge, rather than
living only in that PR's "Known gaps" section and its (now resolved) review
threads.

## The residual gaps

| Gap | Where | What still gets through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extraction race | `Expand` extraction loop | One output can land outside trusted storage if a competing writer wins the race between the identity proof and the create; an ancestor swapped inside the loop is not caught by the leaf-only probe. |
| Directory-creation race | invocation-root / candidate creation | An *empty* directory placed at the chosen name inside the race window is still adopted. |
| Windows root separation (alias -> descendant) | Windows identity chain | An alias mapped to a *descendant* of the checkout is not detected; the canonical spelling cannot express link-ness on Windows. |
| Regular-file-proof -> open window | every opening site | The window between the regular-file proof and the open is not closed (mitigated today by the `0700` invocation root). |

## Why it cannot be closed as written

- Closing the races needs **handle-relative creation with no-follow semantics**
  (open the parent by handle, create relative to it, refuse to follow links).
  Portable .NET does not expose this; Windows PowerShell 5.1 needs P/Invoke.
- Windows link/identity detection needs **handle-based identity**
  (`GetFileInformationByHandleEx`), again P/Invoke on 5.1.
- The only actor who can trigger the races is a **competing untrusted writer**,
  which issue #146 lists under **Non-goals**. So this is a scope question as
  well as an implementation one — the same actor and the same non-goal that make
  `PS-P1A-K-04`'s oracle unreachable (#154).

## What bounds the residual today

Containment and root separation still decide *where* a write may land; the
invocation root is `0700`, so a different unprivileged user cannot reach it; and
the manager's evidence pass refuses at cleanup when the candidate directory
holds anything the ownership journal does not describe. The gaps are exploitable
only by the excluded competing-writer actor.

## Reopen / trigger conditions

Revisit when any of these becomes true:

1. The P1A contract (#146) is revised to admit a bounded competing writer (see
   #154), making the behavior both reachable and in scope; or
2. The minimum supported runtime drops Windows PowerShell 5.1, so a portable
   no-follow / handle-relative API can close the window on every supported
   runtime without per-platform P/Invoke; or
3. P1B (#147) or a later phase adopts a P/Invoke helper, at which point these
   gaps should be closed together.

## References

- PR #153 — "Known gaps -> Security-relevant and open" (the four rows above) and
  the reciprocal P1A<->T1A redline.
- Issue #146 — P1A contract, **Non-goals** ("a competing untrusted writer").
- Issue #154 — the same actor/non-goal makes the `PS-P1A-K-04` oracle unreachable.
- Issue #147 — P1B, the natural home for a shared P/Invoke primitive.
title: Artifact generator and verifier: remaining filesystem race and path-identity limitations

This body applies the already selected post-PR212 F01–F10/A01–A05 amendment after its merge/service-acceptance and independent amendment-review boundary. It does not assert that implementation or acceptance has occurred.

Read current native protections, required check sources and bypasses for the affected repository. Preserve truthful limits: candidate-owned workflows and executor assertions do not provide immutable platform enforcement. This task is read-only. Do not replay the old Actions App bypass or activate settings automatically. If a specific settings mutation remains useful, obtain only exceptional authority actually missing after safe independent readiness work, then perform authorized changes with native readback before any merge that depends on those settings.
